title: Shardscale
status: core + cabinet on main; iterations in PR; dossier is iteration 10
summary: The weigh-house at the Prismheart arcade row, where cut shards are balanced before they are set. A seeded line of shards comes off the cart in order; each one goes on the left pan, the right pan, or onto a small bench for later. The beam may never tip past the cap, and when every shard is on it must rest level within the tolerance. Every line is solvable by construction; the trick is knowing which shard to hold back and when to bring it down. Deterministic per seed, bit-exact between the Python rules, the C++ core and the Unreal cabinet.

mechanics.name: Line
mechanics.text: 8 / 10 / 12 shards with weights 1-9 drawn in order. Setup repeats the draw (up to 50 times) until the exact search finds a level weighing, so the puzzle always has an answer.

mechanics.name: Turn
mechanics.text: The next shard goes left, right or onto the bench (2 / 2 / 3 slots, kept sorted); a benched shard goes left or right on a later turn. Setting and benching each take one turn; a full bench refuses a hold.

mechanics.name: Cap
mechanics.text: After every placement the pans may differ by at most the cap (6 / 5 / 5). Past it the beam tips, the shards slide off and the weighing is lost with score 0.

mechanics.name: Level
mechanics.text: With every shard placed (cart empty, bench empty) the beam must rest within the tolerance (1 / 1 / 0) to win: 10 + 5 per point of slack under the tolerance + 2 per bench slot never used. Otherwise the beam settles askew and the weighing is lost.

mechanics.name: Weigher (demo)
mechanics.text: An exact depth-first search over (shards taken, difference, bench) with actions in the rules' order (left, right, hold, then each bench shard left/right), memoised; it plays the first winning action and levels every seeded line. Lighter-pan greedy that never benches wins only about 12 / 6 / 1 percent, so the bench is the whole skill.

mechanics.name: Preview
mechanics.text: preview(action) gives the difference after, whether it tips and whether it ends the weighing, without moving anything; the native sweep proves it equals the real move. It drives the FITS line and the tip warnings.

mechanics.name: Guide (option 1)
mechanics.text: Practice mode marks the shard the weigher's line takes next (cart or bench) in blue and says which pan or the bench. In both modes the HUD says where the shard in hand fits without tipping, and the hint warns when it fits neither pan.

mechanics.name: Saves
mechanics.text: Text save (shared DaedalusDesktopSaveText shape): difficulty, seed, index, left, right, held, used, hand, score, tipped, over, won. Restore regenerates the line from the seed and checks that pans + bench account for exactly the shards taken, the bench is sorted and within its slots, the beam is within the cap unless tipped, and the flags follow the rules; Python from_state applies the same checks.

mechanics.name: Controls
mechanics.text: Up/Down (or stick) pick the shard in hand: the cart's next shard or a bench shard; Left/Right set it on a pan; A / J / Space bench the next shard; R or pad Start restart a finished weighing. Cabinet class DesktopGames/DaedalusDesktopShardscaleCore.h, registry id shardscale, save slot shardscale.dgs.

items.text: A brass beam on a stone pillar with two hanging pans; it tilts with the difference and drops when it tips.
A cut crystal shard with its weight etched on the face; violet squares on the cart.
The shard cart showing the next five shards in order.
A short stone shelf with 2-3 slots where shards wait; kept in weight order.
The gold frame on the shard about to be set.

storyline.text: Every prism tile in the arcade is balanced before it is set; tonight the master weigher is out and the cart is full.
Three rows on the first shard: Left/Right set the shard in hand, past the cap the beam tips, place every shard and end level. (They leave after the first shard.)
Each difficulty is a longer line with a tighter beam: 8 shards with cap 6 and tolerance 1, 10 shards with cap 5, then 12 shards that must end exactly level, with a third bench slot to plan around.
The last shard settles and the beam rests level; every point of slack and every bench slot left clean is the weigher's thanks.
The beam tips and the shards slide off, or the last shard leaves it askew. Pad A or R rolls the same line again so the holds can be learned.
The weigh-house sits at the end of the Prismheart arcade row after the kite anchor; a side craft, not a campaign gate, and level weighings add to the arcade scoreboard.
